Building and testing the project depends on the components involved and the platform where development is taking place. Due to the amount of context required it's usually best not to try building or testing the project unless the user requests it. If you must build the project then inspect the Makefile in the project root and the Makefiles of any backends that are effected by changes you are making. In addition the workflows in .github/workflows can be used as a reference when it is unclear how to build or test a component. The primary Makefile contains targets for building inside or outside Docker, if the user has not previously specified a preference then ask which they would like to use.

## Building a specified backend

Let's say the user wants to build a particular backend for a given platform. For example let's say they want to build coqui for ROCM/hipblas

- The Makefile has targets like `docker-build-coqui` created with `generate-docker-build-target` at the time of writing. Recently added backends may require a new target.
- At a minimum we need to set the BUILD_TYPE, BASE_IMAGE build-args
  - Use `.github/backend-matrix.yml` as a reference — it's the data-only YAML that lists every backend variant's `build-type`, `base-image`, `platforms`, etc. (`backend.yml` and `backend_pr.yml` consume it via `scripts/changed-backends.js`).
  - l4t and cublas also require the CUDA major and minor version.
  - For llama-cpp / ik-llama-cpp / turboquant the matrix also sets `builder-base-image` pointing at a prebuilt `quay.io/go-skynet/ci-cache:base-grpc-*` tag. Local `make backends/<name>` defaults to `BUILDER_TARGET=builder-fromsource` and doesn't need it — the Dockerfile's from-source stage installs everything itself.
- You can pretty print a command like `DOCKER_MAKEFLAGS=-j$(nproc --ignore=1) BUILD_TYPE=hipblas BASE_IMAGE=rocm/dev-ubuntu-24.04:7.2.1 ROCM_PACKAGES="hipblas-dev hipblaslt-dev rocblas-dev" make docker-build-coqui` (coqui is a Python backend, which stays on ROCm 7.2.1; for Go/C++ backends use `BASE_IMAGE=rocm/dev-ubuntu-24.04:10.1.0-full` and the default `ROCM_PACKAGES`)
- Unless the user specifies that they want you to run the command, then just print it because not all agent frontends handle long running jobs well and the output may overflow your context
- The user may say they want to build AMD or ROCM instead of hipblas, or Intel instead of SYCL or NVIDIA insted of l4t or cublas. Ask for confirmation if there is ambiguity.
- Sometimes the user may need extra parameters to be added to `docker build` (e.g. `--platform` for cross-platform builds or `--progress` to view the full logs), in which case you can generate the `docker build` command directly.

## Test coverage gate

The core Go suites (`./pkg`, `./core`, plus the in-process integration suite `./tests/e2e`) are covered by a **strict, monotonic coverage ratchet**:

- `make test-coverage` — runs the suites with `covermode=atomic` instrumentation and writes a merged profile to `coverage/coverage.out`. Uses the same prerequisites as `make test`.
  - **`--coverpkg` (`COVERAGE_COVERPKG = core/...,pkg/...`):** coverage is attributed to the core+pkg packages, not just the package under test. The React UI (`core/http/react-ui/`) has **no component/unit tests** — its only tests are the Playwright e2e specs in `e2e/`, which run against the real app served by `tests/e2e-ui/ui-test-server` (the dist is `//go:embed`ed, so the server is rebuilt per coverage run).
```
root = true

[*]
indent_style = space

[*.go]

[Makefile]

[*.py]
```

- Use comments sparingly to explain why code does something, not what it does. Comments are there to add context that would be difficult to deduce from reading the code.

## Logging

Use `github.com/mudler/xlog` for logging which has the same API as slog.

## Go tests

All Go tests — including backend tests — must use [Ginkgo](https://onsi.github.io/ginkgo/) (v2) with Gomega matchers, not the stdlib `testing` package with `t.Run` / `t.Errorf`. A test file should register a suite with `RegisterFailHandler(Fail)` in a `TestXxx(t *testing.T)` bootstrap and use `Describe`/`Context`/`It` blocks for the actual cases. Look at any existing `*_test.go` under `core/` or `pkg/` for a template.

Do not mix styles within a package. If you are extending tests in a package that already uses Ginkgo, keep using Ginkgo. If you find stdlib-style Go tests in the tree, treat them as tech debt to be migrated rather than as a pattern to follow.

This is enforced by `golangci-lint` via the `forbidigo` linter (see `.golangci.yml`); calls like `t.Errorf` / `t.Fatalf` / `t.Run` / `t.Skip` / `t.Logf` are flagged. Run `make lint` locally before submitting; the same check runs in CI (`.github/workflows/lint.yml`).

## Sentences the host writes to a chat

A sentence that the host (not the model) writes to a person in a messaging chat is a key in
`core/services/studio/hostmsg/locales/*.json`, with a template for each of the six languages
(`en`, `it`, `de`, `es`, `fr`, `pt-BR`), and is written with `msg` or a `hostmsg.Voice` in
`core/services/studio`. Do not pass a fixed English string to `say`, `Post` or `Outgoing`:
`hostmsg_guard_test.go` fails. The catalog test checks that every key has every language and
the same `{placeholders}`. Text for the model (tool descriptions, notes of a turn) stays English
and is not in the catalog.

## Outbound HTTP

All outbound HTTP must go through `github.com/mudler/LocalAI/pkg/httpclient` rather than the standard library's default client. Use `httpclient.New(...)` (no body deadline — safe for streaming/SSE) or `httpclient.NewWithTimeout(d, ...)` (simple request/response). Both **refuse redirects by default** and set a TLS 1.2 floor.

The reason is GHSA-3mj3-57v2-4636: the std default client follows redirects, and on a *cross-host* redirect Go forwards custom credential headers (e.g. Anthropic's `x-api-key`) to the redirect target, leaking the secret. `httpclient` fails closed instead.

- Need to follow redirects (download CDNs, registry blobs, GitHub asset URLs)? Pass `httpclient.WithFollowRedirects()` — it still strips credential headers on any cross-host hop.
- Fetching from a fixed upstream that redirects to a known CDN (a GitHub release asset redirects to its object store)? Pass `httpclient.WithRedirectHosts(hosts...)`: it follows only https hops to the listed hosts, checks every hop against the external URL policy, and drops the request headers on a hop to another origin.
- Have a custom transport (IP-pinned dialer, HTTP/2 tuning, a credential-injecting `RoundTripper`)? Pass `httpclient.WithTransport(rt)`, basing the transport on `httpclient.HardenedTransport()` to keep the TLS floor. Handed a `*http.Client` by a library? `httpclient.Harden(c)` applies the policy in place.

This is enforced by `forbidigo` (see `.golangci.yml`): `http.DefaultClient` and `http.Get`/`Post`/`PostForm`/`Head` are flagged. The `&http.Client{}` composite literal can't be matched precisely by forbidigo without also flagging legitimate `*http.Client` type references, so that form is caught by review — don't construct raw clients.

## Documentation

The project documentation is located in `docs/content`. When adding new features or changing existing functionality, it is crucial to update the documentation to reflect these changes. This helps users understand how to use the new capabilities and ensures the documentation stays relevant.

- **Docs-with-code rule**: When you change user-facing behavior (API endpoints, CLI flags, config keys, or features), update the corresponding page under `docs/content/` in the SAME change, not as a follow-up. A user-facing change without a matching docs update is incomplete. The PR template carries a checklist item for this.
- **Feature Documentation**: If you add a new feature (like a new backend or API endpoint), create a new markdown file explaining what it is, how to configure it, and how to use it. Put it where the reader looks for it: `docs/content/features/` for a task you do in LocalAI, `docs/content/models/capabilities/` for what a kind of model does, `docs/content/models/engines/` for a backend with its own page, and `docs/content/addons/catalogue/` for an add-on. Add the page to the front door of its section.
- **Configuration**: If you modify configuration options, update the relevant sections in `docs/content/`.
- **Examples**: providing concrete examples (like YAML configuration blocks) is highly encouraged to help users get started quickly.
- **Shortcodes**: Use `{{% callout style="note" %}}`, `{{% callout style="tip" %}}`, `{{% callout style="warning" %}}` or `{{% callout style="info" %}}` for callout boxes, and close them with `{{% /callout %}}`. The `notice` shortcode is deprecated in the Relearn theme and prints a build warning. Give each `tab` a `title=` (the `name=` parameter is deprecated). Write `{{% relref "..." %}}` with `%`, not `<`. Do **not** use `{{% alert %}}`: that shortcode does not exist in this project's Hugo theme and breaks the docs build.

## React UI styling

The React UI ships a design system in `core/http/react-ui/src/App.css`: design
tokens, form grids, data tables, stat cards, callouts, plus a small semantic
primitive layer (`.stack`, `.hstack`, `.text-note`, `.text-meta`, `.tone-*`,
`.icon-chip`). **Use it instead of `style={{ ... }}`.** Inline styles are a
spacing or colour decision made in one file, so no two pages end up sharing a
rhythm, which is the main reason the app reads as unfinished.

Inline styles are still correct for values that are genuinely computed at
runtime: `width: ${pct}%`, a data-driven `background`, a tooltip's coordinates.
Everything else belongs in a class.

A ratchet enforces this:

```sh
cd core/http/react-ui
npm run lint:inline-styles          # fails if the count went UP
npm run lint:inline-styles:report   # per-file counts, worst first
npm run lint:inline-styles:write    # refresh the baseline after converting
```

The gate also fails on **duplicate `className` attributes on one element**. JSX
keeps the last and silently drops the first, so `<i className={icon}
className="text-xs" />` loses its icon while passing lint, the build and the e2e
suite. Converting a style to a class on an element that already has a
`className` is the usual way to introduce one; merge them into a single
attribute instead.

When converting a page, prefer naming the shapes it actually has
(`.p2p-diagram`, `.usage-tile`) over adding more utilities, and check whether an
existing block already covers it: the Nodes page reuses the P2P setup shapes,
and Model Editor reuses the Settings section rail.

Let's say the user wants to build a particular backend for a given platform. For example let's say they want to build coqui for ROCM/hipblas

- At a minimum we need to set the BUILD_TYPE, BASE_IMAGE build-args
  - Use `.github/backend-matrix.yml` as a reference — it's the data-only YAML that lists every backend variant's `build-type`, `base-image`, `platforms`, etc. (`backend.yml` and `backend_pr.yml` consume it via `scripts/changed-backends.js`).

## Logging

Use `github.com/mudler/xlog` for logging which has the same API as slog.

## Go tests

All Go tests — including backend tests — must use [Ginkgo](https://onsi.github.io/ginkgo/) (v2) with Gomega matchers, not the stdlib `testing` package with `t.Run` / `t.Errorf`. A test file should register a suite with `RegisterFailHandler(Fail)` in a `TestXxx(t *testing.T)` bootstrap and use `Describe`/`Context`/`It` blocks for the actual cases. Look at any existing `*_test.go` under `core/` or `pkg/` for a template.

Do not mix styles within a package. If you are extending tests in a package that already uses Ginkgo, keep using Ginkgo. If you find stdlib-style Go tests in the tree, treat them as tech debt to be migrated rather than as a pattern to follow.

This is enforced by `golangci-lint` via the `forbidigo` linter (see `.golangci.yml`); calls like `t.Errorf` / `t.Fatalf` / `t.Run` / `t.Skip` / `t.Logf` are flagged. Run `make lint` locally before submitting; the same check runs in CI (`.github/workflows/lint.yml`).

## Sentences the host writes to a chat

A sentence that the host (not the model) writes to a person in a messaging chat is a key in

(`en`, `it`, `de`, `es`, `fr`, `pt-BR`), and is written with `msg` or a `hostmsg.Voice` in
`core/services/studio`. Do not pass a fixed English string to `say`, `Post` or `Outgoing`:
`hostmsg_guard_test.go` fails. The catalog test checks that every key has every language and
the same `{placeholders}`. Text for the model (tool descriptions, notes of a turn) stays English
and is not in the catalog.

## Outbound HTTP

All outbound HTTP must go through `github.com/mudler/LocalAI/pkg/httpclient` rather than the standard library's default client. Use `httpclient.New(...)` (no body deadline — safe for streaming/SSE) or `httpclient.NewWithTimeout(d, ...)` (simple request/response). Both **refuse redirects by default** and set a TLS 1.2 floor.

The reason is GHSA-3mj3-57v2-4636: the std default client follows redirects, and on a *cross-host* redirect Go forwards custom credential headers (e.g. Anthropic's `x-api-key`) to the redirect target, leaking the secret. `httpclient` fails closed instead.

- Need to follow redirects (download CDNs, registry blobs, GitHub asset URLs)? Pass `httpclient.WithFollowRedirects()` — it still strips credential headers on any cross-host hop.
- Fetching from a fixed upstream that redirects to a known CDN (a GitHub release asset redirects to its object store)? Pass `httpclient.WithRedirectHosts(hosts...)`: it follows only https hops to the listed hosts, checks every hop against the external URL policy, and drops the request headers on a hop to another origin.
- Have a custom transport (IP-pinned dialer, HTTP/2 tuning, a credential-injecting `RoundTripper`)? Pass `httpclient.WithTransport(rt)`, basing the transport on `httpclient.HardenedTransport()` to keep the TLS floor. Handed a `*http.Client` by a library? `httpclient.Harden(c)` applies the policy in place.

This is enforced by `forbidigo` (see `.golangci.yml`): `http.DefaultClient` and `http.Get`/`Post`/`PostForm`/`Head` are flagged. The `&http.Client{}` composite literal can't be matched precisely by forbidigo without also flagging legitimate `*http.Client` type references, so that form is caught by review — don't construct raw clients.

## Documentation

The project documentation is located in `docs/content`. When adding new features or changing existing functionality, it is crucial to update the documentation to reflect these changes. This helps users understand how to use the new capabilities and ensures the documentation stays relevant.

- **Docs-with-code rule**: When you change user-facing behavior (API endpoints, CLI flags, config keys, or features), update the corresponding page under `docs/content/` in the SAME change, not as a follow-up. A user-facing change without a matching docs update is incomplete. The PR template carries a checklist item for this.
- **Feature Documentation**: If you add a new feature (like a new backend or API endpoint), create a new markdown file explaining what it is, how to configure it, and how to use it. Put it where the reader looks for it: `docs/content/features/` for a task you do in LocalAI, `docs/content/models/capabilities/` for what a kind of model does, `docs/content/models/engines/` for a backend with its own page, and `docs/content/addons/catalogue/` for an add-on. Add the page to the front door of its section.
- **Configuration**: If you modify configuration options, update the relevant sections in `docs/content/`.
- **Examples**: providing concrete examples (like YAML configuration blocks) is highly encouraged to help users get started quickly.
- **Shortcodes**: Use `{{% callout style="note" %}}`, `{{% callout style="tip" %}}`, `{{% callout style="warning" %}}` or `{{% callout style="info" %}}` for callout boxes, and close them with `{{% /callout %}}`. The `notice` shortcode is deprecated in the Relearn theme and prints a build warning. Give each `tab` a `title=` (the `name=` parameter is deprecated). Write `{{% relref "..." %}}` with `%`, not `<`. Do **not** use `{{% alert %}}`: that shortcode does not exist in this project's Hugo theme and breaks the docs build.

## React UI styling

The React UI ships a design system in `core/http/react-ui/src/App.css`: design
tokens, form grids, data tables, stat cards, callouts, plus a small semantic
primitive layer (`.stack`, `.hstack`, `.text-note`, `.text-meta`, `.tone-*`,
`.icon-chip`). **Use it instead of `style={{ ... }}`.** Inline styles are a
spacing or colour decision made in one file, so no two pages end up sharing a
rhythm, which is the main reason the app reads as unfinished.

Inline styles are still correct for values that are genuinely computed at
runtime: `width: ${pct}%`, a data-driven `background`, a tooltip's coordinates.
Everything else belongs in a class.

A ratchet enforces this:

```sh
cd core/http/react-ui
npm run lint:inline-styles          # fails if the count went UP
npm run lint:inline-styles:report   # per-file counts, worst first
npm run lint:inline-styles:write    # refresh the baseline after converting
```

The gate also fails on **duplicate `className` attributes on one element**. JSX
keeps the last and silently drops the first, so `<i className={icon}
className="text-xs" />` loses its icon while passing lint, the build and the e2e
suite. Converting a style to a class on an element that already has a
`className` is the usual way to introduce one; merge them into a single
attribute instead.

When converting a page, prefer naming the shapes it actually has
(`.p2p-diagram`, `.usage-tile`) over adding more utilities, and check whether an
existing block already covers it: the Nodes page reuses the P2P setup shapes,
and Model Editor reuses the Settings section rail.

```go
func (l *Ledger) Admit(ctx, req, policy) (*Reservation, error) {
  l.admitMu.Lock(); defer l.admitMu.Unlock()
  for attempt := 0; attempt < maxRounds; attempt++ {
     l.mu.Lock()
     decision := l.decideLocked(req)
     if decision.admit { reserve; l.mu.Unlock(); return res,nil }
     l.mu.Unlock()
     if !decision.reclaimPossible { record rejection; return nil, rejectionErr }
     // serialize eviction
     l.reclaimMu.Lock()
     // someone else may have freed/changed; recompute under mu
     l.mu.Lock(); decision = l.decideLocked(req); ...
     if now admit { reserve; unlock both ... }
     targets := l.selectLocked(decision) // mark evicting
     l.mu.Unlock()
     l.evict(targets) // calls Reclaimer; Forget removes entries
     l.reclaimMu.Unlock()
  }
  record rejection; return err
}
```

The task (Chinese) asks for a unified memory/residency accounting & admission system in LocalAI:

1. Resident ledger: per loaded model an entry with breakdown weights / context cache / attachments (measured, estimated from metadata, or unknown).
2. Same model referenced via alias or multi-level fallback counted once.
3. Aggregates & headroom: per device VRAM and host RAM: resident total, in-flight reservations, limit, remaining.
4. Load admission: before load compute resident + in-flight + pending; over limit → reclaim and recompute; still not enough → reject, before starting the process.
5. Reclaim: LRU or largest-first, bounded attempts/time, skip pinned/busy.
6. In-flight reservations: from admission pass to load end; on success post measured; on failure/cancel/timeout release immediately.
7. Multi-candidate engines: try admissible candidates first; skip candidates that don't fit without starting a process and record the reason; when all rejected return per-candidate reasons.
8. Observability: resident view with per-model ledger entries, aggregate, limit, headroom, in-flight reservations, and recent rejection reasons.
9. Unload/evict/crash/backend unreachable release ledger & reservations within bounded time.

Hard constraints:
1. Ledger host-unique, single write point: load/unload/evict/calibrate all go through one record path, others read-only.
2. Reservation and reclaim mutually exclusive: two concurrent loads each individually fit but together don't must not both pass; no double-count of the same headroom.
3. Limit resolution stable: percentage from detected capacity; absolute must not exceed detected capacity; unset/zero/parse failure must not degrade to zero limit rejecting all loads.
4. Honest provenance: measured vs estimated labeled separately; unknown vs zero distinct; rejection reasons only model name, provenance and byte delta, no weight paths, download URLs, or credential-bearing remote addresses.
5. Default behavior unchanged: no limit → no rejection and no new eviction; when enabled still respects pinned, concurrency-group exclusivity, and existing count limit.

Failure/degradation:
1. When estimate unavailable (remote unreachable, non-weight file, metadata missing) admit as unknown + warn; don't reject.
2. Empty reclaimable set or all serving → explicit rejection naming occupancy models and shortfall bytes, not a backend process started and then killed.
3. Load failure/cancel → reservation returned immediately; retry sees true headroom.
4. Periodic reclaim and admission at same time → only one evicts; same model not evicted twice; calibration failure doesn't affect loaded models.

Existing behavior must not break:
1. Existing count limit, pinned models, concurrency-group eviction order & log semantics unchanged.
2. `/system` and model list fields & null semantics unchanged; new info only additive.

The task in Chinese: implement a unified memory-residency ledger/admission semantics for LocalAI. Requirements:

1. Resident ledger: one entry per loaded model, with components (weights, context cache, attachments) and provenance (measured, estimated, unknown).
2. Same model referenced via alias or multi-level fallback counted once (canonical key).
3. Aggregates by device and host memory: resident total, in-flight reservations, limit, remaining.
4. Load admission: before load compute resident + reserved + pending; over limit → reclaim then recompute; still not enough → reject BEFORE spawning the process.
5. Reclaim: LRU or largest-first, with attempt/time budget, skip pinned/serving.
6. In-flight reservations: from admission to load completion; on success recorded by measurement, on failure/cancel/timeout returned immediately.
7. Multi-candidate engines: prefer candidates that can be admitted; ones that don't fit are not started and the reason recorded; if all rejected, return per-candidate reason list.
8. Observability: resident view gives per-model entries, aggregate, limit, remaining, reservations, recent rejections.
9. Unload/evict/crash/backend-lost release entries and reservations in bounded time.

Hard constraints:
1. Ledger host-unique, single write point: load, unload, evict, calibrate go through one record path; others read-only.
2. Reservation and reclaim mutual exclusion: two concurrent loads each fit but not together must not both be admitted, no double reservation of same headroom.
3. Limit resolution stable: ratio of detected capacity; absolute not exceed detected; unset/zero/parse failure never degrade to zero limit rejecting all loads.
4. Honest provenance: measured vs estimated labeled; unknown vs zero distinguished; reject reasons only model name, provenance and byte shortfall, no weight paths/download URLs/remote addresses with creds.
5. Default behavior unchanged: no limit → neither reject nor add evictions; when on, still respect pinned, concurrency groups, existing count limits.

Failure/degradation:
1. Estimate unavailable (remote unreachable, non-weight file, missing metadata) → admit as unknown with warning, don't reject.
2. Empty reclaimable set or all serving → explicit rejection with the occupying models and byte shortfall, not backend process start then kill.
3. Load failure/cancel → reservation returned immediately; retry sees real headroom.
4. Periodic reclaim + admission concurrently → only one evicts; same model not evicted twice; calibration failure doesn't affect loaded models.

Must not break existing:
1. Existing count limit, pinned, concurrency group eviction order/log semantics unchanged.
2. /system and model list fields/null semantics unchanged, additions only as extra fields.
3. Existing estimate API and budget settings validation unchanged.
4. Distributed multi-node placement unaffected; single-host ledger must not change remote model placement.

You can also configure retry behavior when models are busy:

```bash
# Allow up to 2 active backends with custom retry settings
LOCALAI_MAX_ACTIVE_BACKENDS=2 \
LOCALAI_LRU_EVICTION_MAX_RETRIES=50 \
LOCALAI_LRU_EVICTION_RETRY_INTERVAL=2s \
./local-ai
```

Or using command line flags:

```bash
./local-ai \
  --max-active-backends=2 \
  --lru-eviction-max-retries=50 \
  --lru-eviction-retry-interval=2s
```

This configuration:
- Limits to 2 active backends
- Will retry eviction up to 50 times if models are busy
- Waits 2 seconds between retry attempts
- Ensures busy models have time to complete their requests before eviction

## VRAM Budget (Allocation Ceiling)

By default LocalAI treats **all** detected GPU memory as available for model allocation. On a shared machine (a desktop you also game on, a box that runs other GPU workloads, or a multi-tenant server) you often want to reserve some headroom and let LocalAI use only part of the card. The **VRAM budget** sets a hard ceiling on how much VRAM LocalAI will consider allocatable.

### Configuration

Set the budget with a CLI flag or environment variable:

```bash
# Percentage of detected VRAM
./local-ai --vram-budget=80%

# Absolute amount (GB, GiB, MB, or raw bytes)
./local-ai --vram-budget=12GB

# Using environment variables
LOCALAI_VRAM_BUDGET=80% ./local-ai
LOCALAI_VRAM_BUDGET=12GB ./local-ai
```

Accepted formats:

- A **percentage** such as `80%` (or the decimal `0.8`).
- An **absolute amount** such as `12GB`, `12GiB`, `12000MB`, or a raw byte count.

Leaving it empty or unset (the default) uses all detected VRAM, which is the historical behavior.

### Semantics

The budget is a **hard ceiling**, never a floor:

- Everywhere LocalAI reads VRAM to decide model allocation (hardware defaults for batch size and parallelism, context auto-fit, GGUF fit warnings, and the watchdog), it uses `min(detected VRAM, budget)`.
- The budget can only **lower** usable VRAM, never raise it above what the hardware physically has. An absolute value larger than physical VRAM is clamped to physical.
- A percentage above `100%` is rejected as invalid.

### Editing from the UI

The budget is exposed in the **Settings** page under the **Performance** section as **VRAM Budget**, so you can change it without editing flags or restarting from scratch. It is live-editable and persists to the runtime settings.

### Distributed mode

The same `LOCALAI_VRAM_BUDGET` / `--vram-budget` applies to distributed worker nodes (`local-ai worker ...`), where it caps the VRAM the scheduler will use for per-node placement. Admins can also set a per-node budget live from the node UI (or the admin API); see [Distributed Mode]({{%relref "/administration/distributed-mode#per-node-vram-budget" %}}).

## Limitations and Considerations

### VRAM Usage Estimation

LocalAI cannot reliably estimate VRAM usage of new models to load across different backends (llama.cpp, vLLM, diffusers, etc.) because:
- Different backends report memory usage differently
- VRAM requirements vary based on model architecture, quantization, and configuration
- Some backends may not expose memory usage information before loading the model

### Manual Management

If automatic management doesn't meet your needs, you can manually stop models using the LocalAI management API:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/backend/shutdown \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "model-name"}'
```

To stop all models, you'll need to call the endpoint for each loaded model individually, or use the web UI to stop all models at once.

Conversely, you can pre-load a model into memory ahead of its first request with `POST /backend/load` (the inverse of shutdown) - see [Backend Monitor]({{%relref "/administration/backend-monitor" %}}).

### Best Practices

1. **Monitor VRAM usage**: Use `nvidia-smi` (for NVIDIA GPUs) or similar tools to monitor actual VRAM usage
2. **Set an appropriate backend limit**: For single-GPU systems, `--max-active-backends=1` is often the simplest solution. For systems with more VRAM, you can increase the limit to keep more models loaded
3. **Combine LRU with watchdog**: Use `--max-active-backends` to limit the number of loaded models, and enable idle watchdog to unload models that haven't been used recently
4. **Tune watchdog timeouts**: Adjust timeouts based on your usage patterns - shorter timeouts free memory faster but may cause more frequent reloads
5. **Consider model size**: Ensure your VRAM can accommodate at least one of your largest models
6. **Use quantization**: Smaller quantized models use less VRAM and allow more flexibility

## VRAM estimates in the model gallery

The model gallery shows an estimated VRAM footprint per model, at several
context lengths, so you can see whether something will run before installing it.

Working that out means reading the metadata of a model's weight files, which for
a model you have not installed is a request to the host that serves them. It
takes a second or two the first time, and the gallery needs one per row. LocalAI

Let me look at how the load path could get the model config (for estimation) — currently `model.Options` carries `modelSizeBytes` only. To compute the "pending load" footprint (weights + context cache + attachments), I need the model config or at least the estimate. The `core/backend/options.go` computes `estimateModelSizeBytes` — that returns SizeBytes only (weights file sizes). I need footprint estimate including KV cache.

Where's the right seam? The core/backend is where model config is available. I can add a `WithModelMemoryFootprint` option carrying a richer descriptor: weights bytes, kv cache bytes (estimated), attachments bytes, whether measured or estimated, plus a stable "budget key" (the model's resolved config name for alias dedupe).

Given the enormous scope, I need to design carefully and pragmatically. Let me now plan the architecture.

## Design

New package: `pkg/model/residency` — the ledger/admission semantics. Or put in `pkg/residency`. It must be host-unique, single write point.

Core pieces:

1. **Ledger entries** (`pkg/residency`):
```go
type Determinacy string // "measured", "estimated", "unknown"
type Component struct { Bytes uint64; Determinacy Determinacy; Source string }
type Account struct {
   ModelKey string   // canonical resolved model identity (alias-resolved), for dedupe
   ModelID string    // display name(s)
   Addresses []string
   Weights, ContextCache, Attachments Component
   ...
}
```
Total = sum of determined components + unknown flag.

2. **Ledger** `residency.Ledger`:
- `mu sync.Mutex`
- `devices` (GPU) aggregate and host (RAM) aggregate
- `limits` resolved from budget: device total, host total, per-scope cap
- `entries map[string]*Account` keyed by canonical model key (host-unique)
- `reservations map[string]*Reservation`
- recent rejections ring buffer.
- Single write path: `RecordLoad`, `RecordUnload`, `RecordEviction`, `Calibrate` all go through internal `write*` methods. Read-only: `Snapshot()`.

3. **Admission**: `Admit(req Request) (Reservation, error)`.
- compute scope usage = resident + in-flight reservations.
- If fits → reserve, return.
- Else reclaim: pick candidates per policy (LRU or largest-first), skip pinned/busy, bounded by count and time budget. Recompute. If still insufficient → *IfOverflow else also may be allowed if `AllowUnknown`.
- Must hold a mutex across check+reserve so two loads can't both pass (hard constraint #2).

```go
func (m *Manager) reclaim(ctx, scope, deficit, skip) (freed uint64, evicted []string, err error) {
  if m.reclaimer == nil { return 0,nil,ErrNoReclaimer }
  budgetCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, m.reclaimBudget)
  defer cancel()
  deadline := now+budget
  cands, err := m.reclaimer.Candidates(budgetCtx)
  sort by policy (manager sorts itself to own the policy; reclaimer may pre-sort)
  attempted := map[string]bool
  for _, c := range cands {
     if len(evicted) >= maxEvict { break }
     if budgetCtx.Err() != nil { break }
     if skip[c.Key] || attempted[c.Key] { continue }
     if c.Pinned || (c.Busy && !m.forceBusy) { skipped = append(...) ; continue }
     attempted[c.Key] = true
     before := m.residentBytesLocked(scope)
     stopped, err := m.reclaimer.Evict(budgetCtx, c)
     after := m.residentBytesLocked(scope)
     if stopped && after < before { freed += before-after; evicted=append }
     if freed >= deficit { break }
  }
  return
}
```
Note the manager sorts candidates; policy largest-first uses `c.Bytes` (bytes on scope) or total; LRU uses LastUsed. The reclaimer returns bytes and lastUsed. For `sizeAware` compare c.Bytes.

```go
	m.sweepLocked(now)
	if !m.enabled {
		adm := m.admissionLocked(req, now) // computes figures, allowed

		adm.Reason = ReasonUnknownFootprint

		m.mu.Unlock()
		xlog.Warn(...)

		adm.Allowed = true; adm.Reason = ReasonFits
		res := m.reserveLocked(req, now)
		m.mu.Unlock()
		return res, adm
	} else { adm.Reason = reason }
	m.mu.Unlock()

	// reclaim round
	freed, evicted, blocked, rerr := m.reclaim(ctx, req.Scope, adm.Deficit, map[string]bool{req.Key:true}, req)

	defer m.mu.Unlock()
	m.sweepLocked(m.now())
	adm2 := m.baseAdmissionLocked(req, need, det, now)
	adm2.Evicted = evicted; adm2.Blocked = blocked
	if ok, reason := m.decideLocked(...); ok {
```

This guide covers how to add new API endpoints and properly integrate them with the auth/permissions system.

> **Before you ship a new endpoint or capability surface**, re-read the [checklist at the bottom of this file](#checklist). LocalAI advertises its feature surface in several independent places — miss any one of them and clients/admins/UI won't know the endpoint exists.

## Architecture overview

Authentication and authorization flow through three layers:

1. **Global auth middleware** (`core/http/auth/middleware.go` → `auth.Middleware`) — applied to every request in `core/http/app.go`. Handles session cookies, Bearer tokens, API keys, and legacy API keys. Populates `auth_user` and `auth_role` in the Echo context.
2. **Feature middleware** (`auth.RequireFeature`) — per-feature access control applied to route groups or individual routes. Checks if the authenticated user has the specific feature enabled.
3. **Admin middleware** (`auth.RequireAdmin`) — restricts endpoints to admin users only.

When auth is disabled (no auth DB, no legacy API keys), all middleware becomes pass-through (`auth.NoopMiddleware`).

## Adding a new API endpoint

### Step 1: Create the handler

Write the endpoint handler in the appropriate package under `core/http/endpoints/`. Follow existing patterns:

```go
// core/http/endpoints/localai/my_feature.go
func MyFeatureEndpoint(app *application.Application) echo.HandlerFunc {
    return func(c echo.Context) error {
        // Use auth.GetUser(c) to get the authenticated user (may be nil if auth is disabled)
        user := auth.GetUser(c)

        // Your logic here
        return c.JSON(http.StatusOK, result)
    }
}
```

### Step 2: Register routes

Add routes in the appropriate file under `core/http/routes/`. The file you use depends on the endpoint category:

| File | Category |
|------|----------|
| `routes/openai.go` | OpenAI-compatible API endpoints (`/v1/...`) |
| `routes/localai.go` | LocalAI-specific endpoints (`/api/...`, `/models/...`, `/backends/...`) |
| `routes/studio.go` | Chats endpoints (`/api/chats/...`, including `/api/chats/admin/...` behind the admin middleware) and the agent tasks and jobs (`/api/agent/...`, feature `mcp_jobs`) |
| `routes/auth.go` | Auth endpoints (`/api/auth/...`) |
| `routes/ui_api.go` | UI backend API endpoints |

### Step 3: Apply the right middleware

Choose the appropriate protection level:

#### No auth required (public)
Exempt paths bypass auth entirely. Add to `isExemptPath()` in `middleware.go` or use the `/api/auth/` prefix (always exempt). Use sparingly — most endpoints should require auth.

#### Standard auth (any authenticated user)
The global middleware already handles this. API paths (`/api/`, `/v1/`, etc.) automatically require authentication when auth is enabled. You don't need to add any extra middleware.

```go
router.GET("/v1/my-endpoint", myHandler)  // auth enforced by global middleware
```

#### Admin only
Pass `adminMiddleware` to the route. This is set up in `app.go` and passed to `Register*Routes` functions:

```go
// In the Register function signature, accept the middleware:
func RegisterMyRoutes(router *echo.Echo, app *application.Application, adminMiddleware echo.MiddlewareFunc) {
    router.POST("/models/apply", myHandler, adminMiddleware)
}
```

#### Feature-gated
For endpoints that should be toggleable per-user, use feature middleware. There are two approaches:

**Approach A: Route-level middleware** (preferred for groups of related endpoints)

```go
// In app.go, create the feature middleware:
myFeatureMw := auth.RequireFeature(application.AuthDB(), auth.FeatureMyFeature)

// Pass it to the route registration function:
routes.RegisterMyRoutes(e, app, myFeatureMw)

// In the routes file, apply to a group:
g := e.Group("/api/my-feature", myFeatureMw)
g.GET("", listHandler)
g.POST("", createHandler)
```

**Approach B: RouteFeatureRegistry** (preferred for individual OpenAI-compatible endpoints)

Add an entry to `RouteFeatureRegistry` in `core/http/auth/features.go`. The `RequireRouteFeature` global middleware will automatically enforce it:

```go
var RouteFeatureRegistry = []RouteFeature{
    // ... existing entries ...
    {"POST", "/v1/my-endpoint", FeatureMyFeature},
}
```

A route may have a second row with a **client feature** (`client_self`,
`client_addons`, `client_inference`). A user passes the row of its user feature, and
the key of a paired client passes the row of a feature in its list; a route with no
client row is refused to every client key. The rows of `client_inference` are a
frozen list (spec "freezes the routes of client_inference" in
`core/http/auth/features_client_test.go`): do not add a route to it unless a client
should reach it, and add it to the spec in the same change. A client route needs a
model name in the request. The check that decides is `auth.CheckClientModel`, which
`setModelAndConfig` (and the realtime handshake) calls with the name the handler
resolved, so a route that resolves its model in another place must call it there;
`RequireClientModels` is only the cheap early check and the installer of the gate. A
route without the gate refuses a client key. Test a client route with the real
binder, not with a stub handler (`core/http/middleware/client_models_test.go`).

## Adding a new feature

When you need a new toggleable feature (not just a new endpoint under an existing feature):

### 1. Define the feature constant

Add to `core/http/auth/permissions.go`:

```go
const (
    // Add to the appropriate group:
    // Agent features (default OFF for new users)
    FeatureMyFeature = "my_feature"

    // OR API features (default ON for new users)
    FeatureMyFeature = "my_feature"
)
```

Then add it to the appropriate slice:

```go
// Default OFF — user must be explicitly granted access:
var AgentFeatures = []string{..., FeatureMyFeature}

// Default ON — user has access unless explicitly revoked:
var APIFeatures = []string{..., FeatureMyFeature}
```

### 2. Add feature metadata

In `core/http/auth/features.go`, add to the appropriate `FeatureMetas` function so the admin UI can display it:

```go
func AgentFeatureMetas() []FeatureMeta {
    return []FeatureMeta{
        // ... existing ...
        {FeatureMyFeature, "My Feature", false},  // false = default OFF
    }
}
```

Read this before adding/removing/renaming admin endpoints, MCP tools, or skill recipes.

## What this feature is

`core/services/localaitools/` is a public Go package that exposes LocalAI's admin/management surface as an MCP server. It is used in two ways:

1. **In-process**: when an admin opens a chat with `metadata.localai_assistant=true`, the chat handler injects the in-memory MCP server (paired `net.Pipe()` transport, no HTTP loopback) so the LLM can install models, manage backends and edit configs by chatting.
2. **Standalone**: the `local-ai mcp-server --target=…` subcommand serves the same MCP server over stdio, talking HTTP to a remote LocalAI instance.

The two modes share **all** tool definitions and skill prompts. They differ only in their `LocalAIClient` implementation (`inproc/` calls services directly; `httpapi/` calls REST).

## The three things you must keep in sync

When you change LocalAI's admin surface, three layers must stay aligned:

1. **REST endpoint** in `core/http/endpoints/localai/*.go`.
2. **MCP tool registration** in `core/services/localaitools/tools_*.go`, plus a method on `LocalAIClient` (in `client.go`) and implementations in both `inproc/client.go` **and** `httpapi/client.go`.
3. **Skill prompt** under `core/services/localaitools/prompts/skills/*.md` — the markdown that teaches the LLM how to use the new tool. If the new tool fits an existing recipe, update that recipe; otherwise add a new file.

If you ship a REST endpoint without (2) and (3), conversational admins won't see the feature.

## Checklist for adding a new admin endpoint

- [ ] REST endpoint exists in `core/http/endpoints/localai/*.go` and is gated by `auth.RequireAdmin()` in `core/http/routes/localai.go`.
- [ ] `LocalAIClient` interface in `core/services/localaitools/client.go` has a method covering the new operation.
- [ ] DTOs added/updated in `core/services/localaitools/dto.go` (JSON-tagged; never expose raw service types).
- [ ] `inproc/client.go` implements the new method by calling the service directly (not via HTTP loopback).
- [ ] `httpapi/client.go` implements the new method by calling the REST endpoint.
- [ ] Tool registration added in the appropriate `core/services/localaitools/tools_*.go`. Mutating tools must reference safety rule 1 in the description.

- [ ] Skill prompt added or updated under `core/services/localaitools/prompts/skills/`. The prompt must instruct the LLM when to call the tool, what to ask the user first, and what to do on error.
- [ ] Tests:
   - `core/services/localaitools/server_test.go` adds the tool name to `expectedFullCatalog` and `expectedReadOnlyCatalog` (if read-only).
   - Tool dispatch is added to `TestEachToolDispatchesToClient`.
   - `core/services/localaitools/httpapi/client_test.go` covers the new HTTP path.
- [ ] An admin route or setting that deliberately gets no tool goes in `adminRoutesWithoutTool` in `core/services/localaitools/coverage_test.go`, with the reason. The PR description repeats the reason.

## Adding a new skill recipe (no new tool)

Sometimes you want to teach the LLM a new pattern that uses existing tools. Drop a markdown file under `core/services/localaitools/prompts/skills/<verb>_<noun>.md`. The file is embedded by `//go:embed`. No Go changes needed. It is the **one source** of the recipe, and it reaches the model in two forms:

Each stem comes back as a file.
24:- `speak` (`text`, `voice`, `language`, `format`, `speed`, `instructions`, `sample_rate`, `model`): text to speech, saved as an audio file.
25:- `transcribe_audio`: a recording to text. Use the arguments the tool shows.
26:- `describe_image`: describe an image or answer a question about it, including text in it. Use the arguments the tool shows.
27:- `generate_sound` (`text`, `duration_seconds`, `lyrics`, `instrumental`, `caption`, `bpm`, `keyscale`, `timesignature`, `language`, `vocal_language`, `think`, `do_sample`, `prompt_influence`, `expansion_model`, `model`): a sound effect or music from a description. There is no separate music tool. What you get depends on the installed model: a sound model may make effects only, a song model takes `lyrics`, `caption`, `bpm` and the rest. Say so if the result is not what was asked. It cannot start from an audio file.
28:- `generate_video` (`prompt`, `size`, `seconds`, `fps`, `negative_prompt`, `start_image`, `end_image`, `audio`, `ref_images`, `ref_videos`, `ref_audios`, `seed`, `cfg_scale`, `steps`, `model`): a short video. References (`ref_images`, `ref_audios`, and `ref_videos`, each an object with frames (a list of image files), `fps` and `audio`) do not combine with `start_image` or `end_image`.
29:- `embed` (`input`): vectors for texts, saved as a JSON file. Show the count and size, not the numbers.
30:- `detect` (`image`, `prompt`, `threshold`, `points`, `boxes`): objects with boxes, classes and confidence. `points` (x, y, label 1 or 0) and `boxes` (x1, y1, x2, y2) are flat number lists that prompt segmentation models.
31:- `rerank` (`query`, `documents`, `top_n`): documents ordered by how well they answer the query.
32:- `voice` (`action`, `audio`, `audio2`, `top_k`, `threshold`, `anti_spoofing`): `verify` compares `audio` and `audio2`; `identify` finds who speaks in `audio`.
33:- `face` (`action`, `image`, `image2`, `top_k`, `threshold`, `anti_spoofing`): `verify` compares `image` and `image2` (`anti_spoofing` adds a liveness check); `identify` finds whose face is in `image`.
34:- `voice_profile` (`action`, `name`, `description`, `audio`, `transcript`, `extra_clips`, `language`, `id`): voices that `speak` can clone. `extra_clips` adds more clips of the same voice, each with its own transcript. 35:- `projects` (`action`, `project`, `name`, `description`, `chat_id`, `file`, `content`, `attached`): the user's projects (folders with a shared memory). import (

var _ = Describe("ResidencyViewEndpoint", func() {
	newLoader := func() *model.ModelLoader {
		state, err := system.GetSystemState(system.WithModelPath(GinkgoT().TempDir()))
		Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
		return model.NewModelLoader(state)
	}

	It("reports a disabled view with the resolved limits when no ledger is installed", func() {
		ml := newLoader()
		app := echo.New()
		app.GET("/api/models/residency",
			localai.ResidencyViewEndpoint(ml, &config.ApplicationConfig{}))
		rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
		app.ServeHTTP(rec, httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/api/models/residency", nil))
		Expect(rec.Code).To(Equal(http.StatusOK))
		var view residency.View
		Expect(json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &view)).To(Succeed())
		Expect(view.Enabled).To(BeFalse())
		Expect(view.Note).NotTo(BeEmpty())
	})

	It("reports every account with its provenance and never renders unknown as zero", func() {
		ml := newLoader()
		ledger := residency.NewLedger(residency.Config{
			Host: residency.Limit{CapacityBytes: 16 << 30, CapacityKnown: true,
				LimitBytes: 16 << 30, LimitConfigured: true},
		})
		defer ledger.Close()
		ml.SetResidency(ledger)
		ledger.Settle(residency.Account{
			Model: "measured-model", Pool: residency.PoolHost,
			Weights: residency.Component{Bytes: 4 << 30, Provenance: residency.Measured},
			Context: residency.Component{Bytes: 1 << 30, Provenance: residency.Estimated},
			Extras:  residency.Component{Bytes: 0, Provenance: residency.Estimated},
		})
		ledger.Settle(residency.Account{
			Model: "unknown-model", Pool: residency.PoolHost,
			Weights: residency.Component{Provenance: residency.Unknown},
			Context: residency.Component{Provenance: residency.Unknown},
			Extras:  residency.Component{Provenance: residency.Unknown},
		})

		app := echo.New()
		app.GET("/api/models/residency",
			localai.ResidencyViewEndpoint(ml, &config.ApplicationConfig{}))
		rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
		app.ServeHTTP(rec, httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/api/models/residency", nil))
		Expect(rec.Code).To(Equal(http.StatusOK))

		var view residency.View
		Expect(json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &view)).To(Succeed())
		Expect(view.Enabled).To(BeTrue())
		Expect(view.Accounts).To(HaveLen(2))
		expect := map[string]residency.Provenance{}
		for _, a := range view.Accounts {
			expect[a.Model] = a.Weights.Provenance
		}
		Expect(expect).To(HaveKeyWithValue("measured-model", residency.Measured))
		Expect(expect).To(HaveKeyWithValue("unknown-model", residency.Unknown))
		// The unknown account's charge is not a rendered zero.
		for _, a := range view.Accounts {
			if a.Model == "unknown-model" {
				Expect(a.Charge().Known()).To(BeFalse())
			}
		}
	})
})

		}
		Expect(json.Unmarshal(rec2.Body.Bytes(), &withLedger)).To(Succeed())
		Expect(withLedger.Models).To(ConsistOf(
			HaveKeyWithValue("id", "m"),
		))
		Expect(withLedger.Residency).NotTo(BeNil())
	})
})

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_00_3brfxz8xu2bhwu1qsgeyn5u9","type":"tool_result","content":"## Limitations and Considerations

### VRAM Usage Estimation

LocalAI cannot reliably estimate VRAM usage of new models to load across different backends (llama.cpp, vLLM, diffusers, etc.) because:
- Different backends report memory usage differently
- VRAM requirements vary based on model architecture, quantization, and configuration
- Some backends may not expose memory usage information before loading the model

### Manual Management

If automatic management doesn't meet your needs, you can manually stop models using the LocalAI management API:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/backend/shutdown \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "model-name"}'
```

To stop all models, you'll need to call the endpoint for each loaded model individually, or use the web UI to stop all models at once.

Conversely, you can pre-load a model into memory ahead of its first request with `POST /backend/load` (the inverse of shutdown) - see [Backend Monitor]({{%relref "/administration/backend-monitor" %}}).

### Best Practices

1. **Monitor VRAM usage**: Use `nvidia-smi` (for NVIDIA GPUs) or similar tools to monitor actual VRAM usage
2. **Set an appropriate backend limit**: For single-GPU systems, `--max-active-backends=1` is often the simplest solution. For systems with more VRAM, you can increase the limit to keep more models loaded
3. **Combine LRU with watchdog**: Use `--max-active-backends` to limit the number of loaded models, and enable idle watchdog to unload models that haven't been used recently
4. **Tune watchdog timeouts**: Adjust timeouts based on your usage patterns - shorter timeouts free memory faster but may cause more frequent reloads
5. **Consider model size**: Ensure your VRAM can accommodate at least one of your largest models
6. **Use quantization**: Smaller quantized models use less VRAM and allow more flexibility

## VRAM estimates in the model gallery

The model gallery shows an estimated VRAM footprint per model, at several
as a defensive default, so container startup does not probe remote GGUF files.
Remove that override or set it to a positive number to opt into background
warming.

```bash
# Air-gapped, or you would rather not make the requests at all
LOCALAI_VRAM_WARM_LIMIT=0 local-ai run

# A slow or metered link: warm the same entries, more gently
LOCALAI_VRAM_WARM_CONCURRENCY=1 local-ai run
```

The warm-up never blocks startup, and never fails it: an entry whose weight
files cannot be reached is left cold and estimated later, if anyone asks.

## Related Documentation

- See [Advanced Usage]({{%relref "/models/advanced-usage" %}}) for other configuration options
- See [GPU Acceleration]({{%relref "/models/gpu-acceleration" %}}) for GPU setup and configuration

s=s.replace('''## Limitations and Considerations''','''## Memory admission and the residency ledger

The eviction and budget settings above act *after* the fact: they watch usage
and free models, or cap what the allocation heuristics see. **Memory admission**
adds a pre-load check and an account of what is loaded, so a load that cannot
fit is refused with a byte figure *before* its backend process starts, rather
than left for the operating system to kill.

It is off by default. Turn it on when you want a load to be decided and
explained instead of discovered as a missing process:

```bash
LOCALAI_RESIDENCY_ADMISSION=true \\
LOCALAI_MEMORY_BUDGET=32GB \\
./local-ai
```

### The two pools and their budgets

Every loaded model is charged to exactly one pool:

- **Device** (GPU memory, VRAM): a model with GPU offload (`gpu_layers`,
  `cuda: true` or the `gpu` option).
- **Host** (system RAM): a model that runs on the CPU.

A model served by an external gRPC address on another host is listed but not
charged, so a fleet of remote placements never looks like local pressure.

Each pool has its own budget. `LOCALAI_VRAM_BUDGET` caps the device pool (as
before) and `LOCALAI_MEMORY_BUDGET` caps the host pool, in the same syntax
(`80%` or `12GB`). A percentage is taken of the detected capacity. A cap larger
than the detected capacity is clamped to it. An empty, zero or malformed value
means **no cap**, never a zero cap: a typo can never refuse every load.

{{% callout style="note" %}}
Admission only refuses a load in a pool that has a budget. The pool without a
cap admits everything and never triggers a reclaim, so enabling admission with
no budgets leaves behaviour unchanged; you get the observation view below for
free.
{{% /callout %}}

### What a load does

When admission is on and the pool is capped, a load goes through four steps:

1. **Account.** The model is estimated from its weight files and, when
   available, its GGUF header, split into *weights*, the *context* cache (KV and
   compute buffers) and *extras* (projectors, companions). Each part is labelled
   `measured` (read from a file or the process), `estimated` (derived from
   metadata) or `unknown` (could not be determined). Unknown is never treated as
   zero.
2. **Check.** `resident + in-flight reservations + this load` is compared with
   the pool's limit.
3. **Reclaim.** If it does not fit, loaded models are evicted in the configured
   order (`lru`, the default, or `largest`) within a bounded count and time
   budget, skipping pinned models, models serving a request and models already
   being evicted. The check is re-evaluated after each eviction.
4. **Reserve or refuse.** A load that fits (or that reclaiming makes fit) takes a
   reservation from admission until it settles, so two concurrent loads cannot
   both count the same free bytes. A load that provably cannot fit is refused
   before its process is spawned; the refusal names the model, the provenance of
   its size and the byte shortfall, and never a weight path or download address.

A successful load settles the reservation into one account per model. The same
model reached through several names (aliases, failover, a repeated request) is
one account, never double-counted. When the host can read the backend process's
resident memory, the account is calibrated to the measured figure; otherwise it
keeps the estimate. An unload, an eviction, a crash or a lost backend removes
the account, so the next load sees the real headroom.

{{% callout style="tip" %}}
Estimates are best effort. When a size cannot be determined (a remote file that
is unreachable, a non-weight file, missing metadata) the load is **admitted with
a warning**, not refused: a missing estimate must not fail a load that could
have succeeded. The view below reports that pool's headroom as not known rather
than as a number.
{{% /callout %}}

### Several candidate engines

When a model has no backend pinned, LocalAI tries the installed engines in
order. With admission on, each candidate is offered to the ledger first: an
engine that does not fit is skipped and its process is never started, and the
log records which engine was chosen, what was skipped and why. When no candidate
fits, the error lists every candidate's reason.

### Observing the ledger

`GET /api/models/residency` (admin) returns, in one place:

- each loaded model's account: pool, weights, context and extras with their
  provenance, and the measured figure when known;
- the device and host roll-ups: detected capacity, limit, resident and reserved
  bytes, and headroom (`headroom_known: false` when it cannot be computed);
- in-flight load reservations;
- the most recent admission refusals with their byte shortfall and the models
  that held the room.

`GET /system` gains an additive `residency` block with the same per-pool
roll-up, and each model row gains an additive `residency` entry. When no ledger
is installed the response is exactly what it was before.

### Settings

| Flag | Variable | Default | Meaning |
|------|----------|---------|---------|
| `--residency-admission` | `LOCALAI_RESIDENCY_ADMISSION` | `false` | Check memory before a load and reclaim/refuse accordingly. |
| `--memory-budget` | `LOCALAI_MEMORY_BUDGET` | *(empty)* | Cap host RAM for loaded models (`80%` or `12GB`). |
| `--residency-reclaim-order` | `LOCALAI_RESIDENCY_RECLAIM_ORDER` | `lru` | `lru` or `largest`. |

The Settings page exposes the admission switch, both budgets and the reclaim
order under **Memory**. They apply live, without a restart.

### What stays the same

Admission does not replace the existing controls. The max-active-backends
limit, pinned models and concurrency groups keep their behaviour and their
eviction order; a pre-load reclaim respects pinned and busy models exactly as
the memory reclaimer does. The memory reclaimer's periodic check is routed
through the same ledger while admission is on, so the periodic reclaim and a
load admission never evict the same model. Distributed placement is untouched:
the local ledger never changes where a remote replica is placed.

### New pure package `pkg/residency`
- **`types.go`** — `Provenance` (`measured` / `estimated` / `unknown`), `Component`, `Account` (weights + context cache + extras, each with provenance), `PoolSummary`/`Summary` (per device/host: capacity, limit, resident, reserved, headroom, unknown & partial account lists), `Rejection`, `CandidateDecision`, `AllCandidatesRejectedError`, `View`.

- **`ledger.go`** — single-writer ledger. `Settle` (one write path, alias/repeat-safe), `Alias`, `Calibrate`, `Remove`/`RemoveByAddress`, `Admit` (resident + reserved + requested vs limit, reclaim then re-check, refuse before a process starts), `Reclaim` (periodic), reservations with TTL, and a reader `Snapshot`. An unknown size **admits with a warning**, never refuses. `admitMu` serializes admission and reclaim so two concurrent loads can't take the same bytes and a model is never double-evicted; each candidate is marked before its stop.

### `pkg/model` integration
- `residency.go` / `residency_estimate.go` — estimate per engine from weight files + GGUF header split into weights/context/extras; pool selection (device vs host); pool-aware measurement (DRM VRAM for device, RSS for host) with a plausibility guard; `AdmitCandidates`; evictor that takes the per-model operation lock and only stops the recorded incarnation; release on unload, eviction, crash (`forgetExitedProcess`), and lost backend.
- `initializers.go` — admission runs inside `grpcModel` after every other guard and **before** `spawnGRPCModel`; the trial loop admits each candidate in order, skips the ones that don't fit (never starts them), falls through on a start failure, and returns `AllCandidatesRejectedError` when all are refused. Reservation is threaded through so bytes aren't double-counted.
- `watchdog.go` — a pressure hook so the memory reclaimer's periodic eviction runs through the same ledger mutex/marking.

### Wiring, observation, docs

- Settings UI fields, docs section in `vram-management.md`, runtime-settings docs.
